paper_title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Linear attention scales linearly with sequence length, but its finite-state memory can limit long-context retrieval. In gated linear recurrences, memory retention depends on state decay, which is shaped jointly by gate parameters A_log and dt_bias and by input activations. In controlled Gated DeltaNet (GDN) experiments, both parameters remain highly correlated with their initial values after training, highlighting the importance of initialization. Therefore, we introduce Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI), which jointly configures these parameters before training. DAMI assigns geometric timescales across heads for varied retrieval distances and a low-high-low input-sensitivity profile across layers. A small activation sample calibrates the GDN-family implementation to match both behavioral targets without adding trainable parameters. Across GDN, KDA, GDN2, Mamba-2, and RWKV-7, DAMI improves average RULER-style retrieval accuracy by 5.29 to 16.71 percentage points over the corresponding random-initialization baselines. Performance on language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and 2K real-world retrieval remains broadly comparable to those baselines. Our code is available at https://speedai.com/research/dami.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Long-context retrieval requires retaining distant information despite intervening distractors. Linear attention and gated recurrences replace softmax attentions quadratic computation and growing cache with fixed-size states (Vaswani et al., 2017; Katharopoulos et al., 2020). Retrieval remains challenging even as recurrent architectures advance (Arora et al., 2024a,b; Yang et al., 2025; 1Our code is available at https://speedai.com/ research/dami. Kimi Team, 2025; Hatamizadeh et al., 2026). We investigate decay-gate initialization as means of improving memory without changing state-update operators. In controlled Gated DeltaNet (GDN) runs, the learnable memory parameters A_log and dt_bias remain highly correlated with their initial values (Section 3.2), motivating structured initialization. PoST improves long-range memory through geometric decay spectra and position-adaptive scaling (Cao, 2026). Realized decay, however, depends jointly on the decay multiplier A_log, the Softplus operating region shifted by dt_bias, and input activations. Achieving intended memory behavior therefore requires coordinating both parameters. We propose Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI): geometric target timescales across heads and lowhighlow input-sensitivity profile across layers. Approximate power-law dependencies in text and their exponential-mixture representation motivate multiscale coverage (Altmann et al., 2012; Lin and Tegmark, 2017; Beylkin and Monzón, 2010), while different representation stages motivate depth-dependent responses. Figure 1 illustrates these complementary requirements. DAMI jointly calibrates both targets from actual activations before training. Its GDN-family implementation adjusts native memory parameters; Mamba-2 and RWKV-7 use architecture-specific extensions (Section 3.5). Across approximately 100M-parameter GDN, KDA, GDN2, Mamba-2, and RWKV-7 models trained on 5B tokens, DAMI improves average RULER-style NIAH accuracy (Hsieh et al., 2024) by 5.2916.71 percentage points over Random and outperforms PoST-style spectral initialization. Language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and realworld retrieval remain broadly comparable. Our main contributions are: We identify persistent correlations between initial and trained GDN memory parameters, motivating structured initialization. We introduce DAMI, jointly configuring headwise timescales and layer-wise sensitivities, with extensions to Mamba-2 and RWKV-7. Five-architecture experiments demonstrate improved retrieval with broadly comparable general capabilities; GDN ablations establish the benefit of the joint configuration.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Gated Recurrences and Long-Context Retrieval. Linear attention compresses history into fixedsize state (Katharopoulos et al., 2020). GLA, DeltaNet, and the GDN family improve recurrence through gating and the delta rule (Yang et al., 2024a,b, 2025; Kimi Team, 2025; Hatamizadeh et al., 2026); Mamba develops selective state spaces and state space duality (Gu and Dao, 2024; Dao and Gu, 2024). Zoology and RULER distinguish computational efficiency from effective recall through retrieval evaluations (Arora et al., 2024a; Hsieh et al., 2024). DeciMamba and LongMamba extend receptive fields through post-training filtering (Ben-Kish et al., 2024; Ye et al., 2025). DAMI operates at initialization, leaving the recurrence and inference procedure unchanged. Decay Spectra and Power-Law Dependencies. Multiscale memory has also been explored in dynamic graphs, where hierarchical memories combine continuous-time updates with multiple discrete-time granularities to capture temporal dynamics (Zhang et al., 2022). HiPPO, S4, and S4D connect long-range memory to structured dynamics and spectra (Gu et al., 2020, 2022a,b). Approximate power-law dependencies in text (Altmann et al., 2012; Lin and Tegmark, 2017) motivate exponential mixtures with controlled approximation error (Beylkin and Monzón, 2005, 2010). PoST applies geometric spectra and position-adaptive scaling to linear recurrences (Cao, 2026). Building on this multiscale motivation, DAMI jointly realizes target timescales and input responses in GDN gates. Memory Initialization. Chrono initialization uses anticipated temporal ranges, while LRU combines stable parameterization, eigenvalue initialization, and normalization (Tallec and Ollivier, 2018; Orvieto et al., 2023). LSUV calibrates activation variance sequentially using real samples (Mishkin and Matas, 2016). DAMI uses this layer-sequential approach to calibrate head-wise timescales and layer-wise Softplus sensitivities: it jointly determines A_log and dt_bias before training.

sections.title: 3 Method
sections.content: We formulate head-wise timescales and layer-wise Softplus sensitivities for finite-state recurrences (Katharopoulos et al., 2020; Dao and Gu, 2024), motivated by persistent initialization structure. Figure 2 summarizes their joint calibration in DAMI.

sections.title: 4 Experiments
sections.content: We evaluate retrieval and general capabilities, ablate both initialization axes, and examine retrieval across distances.

sections.title: 4.1 Experimental Setup
sections.content: Models and training. We evaluate GDN (Yang et al., 2025), KDA (Kimi Team, 2025), GDN2 (Hatamizadeh et al., 2026), Mamba-2 (Dao and Gu, 2024), and RWKV-7 (Peng et al., 2025) at approximately 100M parameters, each trained on 5B tokens with maximum context of 4,096 tokens. Within each architecture, comparisons share parameterization and training recipe; GDN-family and Mamba-2 variants preserve Randoms non-decay initialization. RWKV-7 uses the common frozenscale parameterization in Section 3.5; its selected Random/PoST checkpoints use seed 42 and DAMI uses seed 43. Architecture dimensions are in Appendix D. low layer profile (approximately 0.250.750.25 sensitivity for the GDN family). Section 3.5 and Appendix detail the adaptations and configurations. Evaluation protocol. Primary retrieval uses fixed RULER-style NIAH subset (Hsieh et al., 2024): NIAH-1/2 at 1K, 2K, 4K, and 8K; MKNIAH at 1K, 2K, and 4K. All models share 500 pregenerated samples per setting and fixed decoding settings. We report answer-containment accuracy and its unweighted mean over the 11 settings. General-capability evaluations use WikiText (Merity et al., 2017), WinoGrande (Sakaguchi et al., 2020), ARC-Easy/Challenge (Clark et al., 2018), OpenBookQA (Mihaylov et al., 2018), and Social IQa (Sap et al., 2019). Six real-world retrieval tasks at 2K follow BASED/GDN (Arora et al., 2024b; Yang et al., 2025). All evaluations use the same 15 trained checkpoints across five architectures.

sections.title: 5 Conclusion
sections.content: This work presents DAMI, dual-axis memory initialization framework motivated by persistent correlations between initial and trained memory parameters in controlled GDN experiments. DAMI coordinates head-wise timescales and layer-wise input responses through joint calibration for GDN, KDA, and GDN2, with architecture-specific extensions to Mamba-2 and RWKV-7. Experiments across these five recurrent architectures show improved long-context retrieval with broadly comparable language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and real-world retrieval performance. GDN ablations demonstrate the benefit of jointly configuring the two memory parameters. These findings support treating initialization as coordinated design choice for memory behavior, informed by the models actual input activations.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.content: This work focuses on decay-side initialization, coordinating memory timescales and input sensitivities within existing recurrent architectures. Our analysis and experiments characterize this design under each architectures native write parameterization and state-update rules. The write side governs how incoming content is incorporated into the recurrent state, offering complementary perspective on memory formation and its interaction with decay. Future work could jointly study decay-side and write-side initialization to clarify how their coordination balances the incorporation of new information with the retention of useful history.

sections.title: D Detailed Experimental Configurations
sections.content: Model dimensions. All models use hidden size 512 and head dimension 64. GDN, KDA, and GDN2 have 18 layers and six heads, with 103.79M, 101.69M, and 112.25M parameters, respectively; each uses value expansion 2 and width-4 short convolutions. Mamba-2 has 42 layers, 16 heads, and 105.01M parameters, with expansion 2, state size 128, and width-4 convolution. RWKV-7 has 20 layers, eight heads, and 101.43M parameters. Each model is trained on 5B tokens with maximum context of 4,096 tokens. The selected RWKV-7 Random/PoST checkpoints use seed 42, and DAMI uses 43. Initialization settings. The PoST condition uses six-head spectrum spanning 08.318 for the GDN family and 16-head spectrum over the same range for Mamba-2. RWKV-7 retains Randoms channel bias and solves frozen scales for eight geometric timescales. This condition uses spectral initialization only, with no positionadaptive scaling. GDN-family DAMI targets are {4096, 776.05, 147.03, 27.86, 5.28, 1} tokens. Its 18-layer sensitivity profile has endpoints 0.25 and central peak of 0.748. KDA/GDN2 use centered channel perturbations with standard deviation 0.03, aligning within-head means with the GDN target. Mamba-2 resamples the layer multipliers to 42 layers and normalizes their geometric mean to one, as in Appendix C. RWKV-7 uses 0.250.750.25 mean sigmoid-response profile and an eight-head geometric timescale ladder from 4,096 to 1. Distance-based retrieval analysis. Figure 6 uses all 500 samples per tasklength setting. Each bin averages task-specific accuracies with equal weights: NIAH-1, NIAH-2, and MK-NIAH for 1K 4K; NIAH-1 and NIAH-2 for 8K. The 16 shared bins start at equal widths; one boundary is minimally adjusted using sample positions alone to ensure each task contributes to every bin. Points use bin centers.
